idea-plugin.name: PHPGloss
idea-plugin.description:
PhpStorm reads PHPDoc, but not all of it. Type aliases collapse to array, conditional return types come back as both branches at once, and a type variable inside a type argument is never filled in. This plugin resolves those in the IDE, so the type you see matches the type PHPStan infers.

Type aliases

  • Hover a @phpstan-type or @phpstan-import-type alias to see the shape it stands for.
  • Go to Declaration jumps from a reference to its declaration, and from a declaration to its usages.
  • Key access on a shape imported from another file resolves, instead of mixed.
  • Aliases declared on interfaces and traits work the same as on classes.

Type keywords

The 84 keywords PHPStan and Psalm reserve — non-empty-string, positive-int, class-string and the rest — are explained on hover, with Go to Declaration opening the code that defines them. Descriptions are quoted from the upstream classes, and shown in Japanese when the IDE is in Japanese.

Type inference

  • Conditional return types are evaluated against the arguments at the call site, including nested ones.
  • Type variables inside type arguments are resolved, and carried into __invoke.
  • A callable(V, K): E binds E from the closure passed in.
  • Refinements written in @var survive instead of flattening.
  • A branch the arguments cannot decide is left alone — no type is better than a wrong one.

The plugin runs no external process and makes no network request. It does not run PHPStan.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.64.0

  • Do not read the type of an argument that is itself a call. Reading it resolves that expression, which walks back to the outer call and trips PhpStorm's recursion guard; the failure surfaces as `TypeProvider contract violation`, twenty-two of them while indexing a large project — more than every PHP-plugin provider combined. Nested calls like `array_values(Grouping::by(...))` are where it happens. Variables and literals state their own type, so following them does not come back.
  • The two earlier attempts (0.62.0, 0.63.0) narrowed the wrong paths. The condition came from disassembling `PhpTypeInfo`, which wraps whatever a provider throws — the recursion guard was the thrower.

Full history: CHANGELOG.md
